turns.text: /navigator Grill me on how retries work in this repo. Use user style tony.

GRILL_ME on retry behavior, user style `tony`.

I read:
- `src/retry.js` (`withRetry`, `backoffDelay`)
- `src/client.js` (`fetchJson`, `isRetryable`)
- `test/retry.test.js`

First question, big picture:

A server answers 503 to every request. You call `fetchJson(transport, '/items')` with default options. How many times is `transport` called, and what does the caller get in the end?
Four times I think, then it throws.

Correct on both.

- Default `retries` is 3 (`src/retry.js:1`). The first call plus 3 retries makes 4 calls.
- After the fourth failure, `attempt >= retries` is true, so the error is rethrown (`src/retry.js:16`).
- The caller gets the last `HttpError`, with `status` 503 (`src/client.js:18`).
- One detail you skipped: the waits between calls are 100, 200, then 400 ms (`backoffDelay`, `src/retry.js:4`).

Next question:

The server answers 404 on the very first call. How many times is `transport` called, and why?
